position_in_era.historical_role: The song that canonized the suite-structure for mainstream rock: ballad → guitar solo → pseudo-operatic section → hard rock → outro. Brian May's guitar solo (2:37–3:05) explicitly functions as a voice ('I regard the guitar in that situation as a voice') and serves as the hinge between the intimate ballad and the operatic multi-character section. Mercury as aria-voice; May as guitar-protagonist.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Recorded August 24–September 1975 across five studios (Rockfield, Wessex, Sarm East, Olympic, Scorpio). Approximately 180 vocal overdubs for the operatic section, layered until the tape became translucent. May's 9-bar guitar solo bridges the ballad to the opera section; he described wanting to 'sing a verse on the guitar' — the solo is explicitly conceived as a melodic voice.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Freddie Mercury composed the complete piece, describing it as 'basically three songs I wanted to put out.' Brian May's guitar solo was May's autonomous compositional contribution — Mercury specified where it went, May wrote what it played. The operatic section uses May, Mercury, and Roger Taylor's vocals layered 180 times, making the 'other' voice a choir of selves rather than one guitar.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: May: Red Special guitar (custom-built by May and his father) through Vox AC30 amplifiers, using a sixpence coin as a pick. Mercury: Steinway grand piano for the ballad section. The hard rock section uses May's layered guitar army — he tracked multiple rhythm and lead parts to create an orchestral wall.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: The song was declared too long for radio (5:55) by EMI; DJ Kenny Everett played it anyway and demand made it the Christmas No. 1 in the UK for nine weeks. The song demonstrated that a six-minute multi-section piece could be a mainstream hit.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: Single released October 1975; album November 1975. The guitar solo's explicit framing as a voice — 'I sang the verse on the guitar' (May, Guitar World interview, documented) — is the key lineage fact for aria_solo_dialectic.
